recordings.creator: James Ray
recordings.location_evidence:
:
Psophodes olivaceus pair at intervals, loudest 1:32 otherwise contact calls. Edit: soft chortling of eastern whipbird at start, faint (originally unknown), then male call at 0:12, 0:26, 0:36, 0:46, 0:57. Wee-whop wee-whop wow. Sometimes with chip-chip. 1:35.
0:08 descending whistles chee-chiew-chiew-chiew-chiew-chiew. I think it's a brown thornbill.
Acanthorhynchus tenuirostris 1:12, 1:18.
Anthochaera carunculata 0:14, 2:11, 2:46
Myzomela sanguinolenta? Seep-seep-seep-seep at intervals e.g. 0:39, 0:49 (responses to eastern whipbirds). New holland honeyeaters are regularly seen in the area, but AIUI they only make single seep calls. Note that I haven't seen any male Myzomela sanguinolentas (or females, AFAIK), so I'm skeptical about this, but I'll keep an eye out for them.
Menura novaehollandiae 1:05+, 2:11+

recordings.title: Dacelo leachii - Blue-winged Kookaburra XC492215.mp3
recordings.creator: Peter Russell
recordings.location_evidence:
:The Blue-winged Kookaburra males usually start this call right on the first glow of light in the eastern sky and also the last glow of light in the evening . They will use the same call during the day around breeding season to attract mates and let other males know their territory .
Their habitat is mainly  semi-arid country along water ways in the Northern Parts across Australia . They are normally stationary birds do not move very far during the year .
Their food consists of Reptiles- small birds- marsupiales - frogs and large insects .
Their nesting habits are usually hollows in Eucalypt trees and sometimes in cliff faces where small hollows may excist '
They are a very nervous bird and will sit very still in foliage so not to be seen .
